title: Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale (CES-D)
sourceName: National Institutes of Health — CES-D Common Data Element; Copyright: No
citation: Radloff, L. S. (1977). The CES-D Scale: A self-report depression scale for research in the general population. Applied Psychological Measurement, 1(3), 385–401.
prompt: Below is a list of ways you might have felt or behaved. Please indicate how often you felt this way during the past week.
useNotice: Official source documents free use / no copyright claim. This digital version is not independently validated and is not diagnostic. Interpret only within an appropriate clinical, research, or population context.

responseOptions.label: Occasionally or a moderate amount (3–4 days)
Most or all of the time (5–7 days)

questions: I was bothered by things that usually don't bother me.
I did not feel like eating; my appetite was poor.
I felt that I could not shake off the blues even with help from my family or friends.
I felt that I was just as good as other people.
I had trouble keeping my mind on what I was doing.
I felt that everything I did was an effort.
I felt hopeful about the future.
I thought my life had been a failure.
I felt that people disliked me.
scoringNote: Sum 20 responses after reverse-scoring items 4, 8, 12, and 16 (0↔3, 1↔2). Range 0–60. This implementation reports raw score only; cut-offs vary by setting and are not diagnostic.
